content.title: About
content.content: Hunan Beef is a spicy Chinese dish made from thin strips of beef quickly stir‑fried with vegetables, garlic, ginger, and aromatic spices such as Sichuan pepper, soy sauce, and rice vinegar. The dish is known for its bright, slightly sweet flavor and a distinctive “numbing” heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originates from Hunan province, famous for its bold, peppery cuisine.
Traditionally the beef is marinated in soy sauce, corn starch, and rice wine to keep it tender.
Sichuan pepper isn’t a true pepper; its husks create a tingling, numbing sensation on the tongue.
Fermented black beans are often added for extra umami depth.
Cooking is done in a wok over high heat, preserving the crispness of the vegetables.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Iron from beef supports normal hemoglobin levels and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: B‑vitamins, especially B12, aid nervous system function and metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Sichuan pepper and ginger contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Ginger and garlic stimulate gastric juices, promoting better digestion.

items.title: Spicy heat
items.content: Large amounts of heat can cause heartburn or stomach irritation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Beef or spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to beef or ingredients like garlic.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor harmful bacteria; cook until fully done.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Hunan Beef hot, typically over steamed rice or noodles. Add fresh vegetables such as bell pepper and carrot for color and crunch. The dish can be eaten with chopsticks or a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Raw beef should be kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Cooked Hunan Beef can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
